what: American Airlines is one of the three large American network carriers, flying from hubs at Dallas, Charlotte, Miami, Philadelphia, Phoenix and Chicago, with a large AAdvantage loyalty programme.
customers: Leisure and business travellers in the United States and internationally, plus credit card partners buying loyalty points.
money: ticket sales across the domestic and international network
freight and the AAdvantage loyalty programme
moat: Hub airports with slots and gates that cannot be duplicated, and a loyalty programme whose credit card partnership generates billions regardless of how the airline itself performs.
risks: $35.9B of debt, the highest of any American airline, against $5.9B of cash
A $481M net loss, and free cash flow was slightly negative
Its premium cabin and corporate share lag Delta and United, which earn far better margins
opportunities: Analysts see about 21% upside, with 23 covering the stock
The AAdvantage credit card agreement generates several billion dollars a year with no aircraft required
watch: Unit revenue relative to Delta and United, and progress on reducing debt.
